newsitem.title: USA: Earthgrains Q3 profit margins improve.
newsitem.headline: Earthgrains Q3 profit margins improve.

text.p: Earthgrains Co said Monday its third-quarter profit, compared with a pro forma loss a year ago, reflected profit-margin improvement across its businesses.
"Our turnaround progress is on track, and we anticipate additional long-term improvements," Barry Beracha, chairman, said in a statement.
Earlier, Earthgrains reported earnings for the third quarter of $0.91 a share, compared with a year-ago pro forma loss of $0.91 a share.

Earthgrains, a baked goods and refrigerated dough company, said its results reflect the continued benefits of restructuring and consolidation actions, reduced costs, improved operating efficiency and price increases.

"Price increases taken during the year for fresh baked goods have continued to hold," Beracha said. "Additionally, we have been an active participant in industry consolidation and look forward to continuing these efforts."
The third quarter also benefited from typically strong seasonal sales as well as selective price increases for U.S. refrigerated dough products.

Earlier, Earthgrains said it will close its Indianapolis refrigerated dough plant by the end of March and transfer production to a plant in Carrollton, Texas. A spokesman said 215 employees in Indianapolis will be terminated as a result of the plant closing, and five to 10 managers will be relocated.
Earthgrains said it will take a charge of $6 million to $8 million in the fourth quarter for the plant closure.
Earthgrains was spun off from Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc in March, 1996.
